name: Derek Owens
line: Derek Owens teaches by recorded lecture and graded papers. In AMP, assessment and teaching happen at every problem.
description: AMP vs Derek Owens: Derek Owens teaches by recorded lecture, then grades papers. In AMP, assessment, teaching and review are continuous, at every problem.
verdict: In the standard option, Derek Owens teaches each course by recorded lecture, and an instructor grades the homework and tests a student sends in [2]. In AMP, assessment and teaching are continuous. Every answer is checked and explained at once, updates the learner's level and sets the next problem.

reasons.title: Feedback on every answer
reasons.body: After every answer, AMP shows whether it was right, the correct answer and the worked steps. In a Derek Owens course, homework and tests go in by email, fax or mail. A person grades them, and the graded papers come back scanned, by email, to the student and parents [2]. Across 40 studies of computer-based feedback, in many ages and subjects, feedback that explains had the largest average effect [5].

reasons.title: Continuous assessment
reasons.body: AMP has no separate test. It places a learner from their first answers, and every answer after updates the learner's level in that part of math and sets the next problem: new work within reach, a gap to close, or an old skill due back. Derek Owens's FAQ describes no placement test. In the first month a student gets both Regular and Honors work, then picks one [3]. After that, assessment is the course's graded homework and tests, the same ones his in-class students take [2].

reasons.title: The problem is the unit
reasons.body: In AMP, everything hangs off the problem: a hint that gives the first step, a lesson with a worked example, a video lesson, the worked answer afterward, and links to the skills it builds on and leads to. In a Derek Owens course the unit is the recorded lecture. The student fills in a skeleton set of notes and works the example problems as he does, then does the homework [2]. Across 55 studies, from elementary to postsecondary, worked examples improved math performance [6].

reasons.title: Moving on, and going back
reasons.body: In AMP an answer given after a hint or a lesson is marked as helped. A skill counts when the learner gets it right without help, more than once, and repeated misses send practice back to what the skill builds on. Those skills sit on one map, from counting through precalculus. In a Derek Owens course, work counts through graded homework and tests, and the course follows its own sequence of assignments at the pace the family sets [1][2][3].

theirs: Derek Owens offers math and physics courses for homeschool students, through his company, Lucid Education, LLC [1]. The math courses run from Prealgebra to AP Calculus, beside Physical Science, Physics and Computer Science. He also teaches live classes in the Atlanta area [1].

An online lesson is a recorded lecture that matches his live classes [2]. The student fills in a skeleton set of lecture notes and works the example problems as he does. Then come homework and tests, the same ones his in-class students take. Work goes in by email, fax or mail, and the graded papers come back scanned, by email [2]. Students may start any time and set their own pace [1][2].
credit: A teacher explains every lesson himself, and students work the examples beside him in their notes [2].
In the standard option, a person reads and grades the student's written work [2].
An Honors track for a student who finds the Regular work too easy [3].

theirs: We found no outcome study of Derek Owens's courses on its site or in Evidence for ESSA [1][2][3][4].
ours: Two findings bear on this comparison. Across 40 studies of computer-based feedback, in many ages and subjects, feedback that explains had the largest average effect (0.49), against 0.32 for the correct answer alone and 0.05 for right or wrong only [5]. Across 55 studies, from elementary to postsecondary, worked examples improved math performance, with an average effect of g = 0.48 [6]. AMP applies both at every problem.

AMP's own outcome studies are planned: growth on a national test against hours of use, then comparison groups, then randomized trials. Each will be registered before it starts and published whatever it finds. The research behind each part of AMP is in our report, and AMP is open source.

them: You want a teacher's recorded lectures, and a person to grade written work.
amp: You want every answer checked and explained the moment it is given.
You want a hint, a lesson and the worked answer at every problem.
You want learned skills to keep coming back in practice.
Your learner is at different levels in different parts of math.

questions.question: How is AMP different from Derek Owens?
questions.answer: In the standard option, Derek Owens teaches by recorded lecture, and an instructor grades the homework and tests a student sends in [2]. AMP has no separate test: every answer is checked and explained at once and sets the next problem, each problem carries its own teaching, and learned skills return in ordinary practice.

questions.question: Do Derek Owens courses work?
questions.answer: We found no outcome study of Derek Owens's courses on its site or in Evidence for ESSA [1][2][3][4].

questions.question: Can a learner use both?
questions.answer: Yes. They are separate programs. AMP places a learner from their first answers, whatever else they use.
